limitations: Approval covers only src/indexed_stores.cpp, raw SHA-256 5b1278d9f1ba51156844e1f6578f71a56c0bc94eaa0b354efec1350aa325c311, under the frozen contracts; registry integration is not approved.
Original execution used Unicorn 2.1.4; candidate execution used native macOS ARM64 C++20 with AppleClang 21. No native Windows/x86 ABI bridge or whole-game validation is established.

Scope is initialized ordinary RAM in the specified 512-byte arena, object offsets 0..128, and normal returns. Faults, address wrap, MMIO, concurrency, exceptions, complete class layout, EDX effects and flags remain excluded.
Review used supplied material only; hashes and execution bindings were not independently recomputed.
review.summary: Both implementations match the supplied complete instruction slices bound to the pinned DAOrigins.exe SHA-256, RVAs and slice hashes. Low-byte index conversion and unsigned comparison reproduce MOV AL/CMP/JAE; accepted returns zero-extend k, while rejected returns preserve incoming EAX upper 24 bits. Exact word/byte helpers reproduce value truncation and little-endian stores without arena reads or surrounding writes. Bounds remain inside the arena; byte-wise access supports unaligned and overlapping guest storage without host-pointer alias assumptions. Arithmetic, conversions and helper shifts are defined within the contract. Original ECX preservation, nonvolatile preservation and ret 8 are supported by instruction evidence and oracle checks; the C++ interface implements the declared high-level mapping. Supplied verified bindings connect this source and frozen contracts/corpora to successful builds, both synthetic commands, 1304 public and 128 heldout cases per function, and 747 expected negative-control mismatches. These results support scoped approval, not proof of whole-game behavior.

integration_transition.change: Only the two package function statuses change from contracted to implemented. All identity, ABI, source, contract and backend fields remain identical.
